--- Transition Strategy Builder ---
# COMPREHENSIVE SUBSCRIPTION TRANSITION PLAN

---

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This plan orchestrates a 36-month transition from perpetual-license to subscription revenue, targeting:
- **Churn containment:** <20% of installed base (vs. competitor benchmark of ~25%)
- **Subscription penetration:** 60%+ of new bookings by month 12; 75%+ by month 24
- **Revenue stabilization:** Inflection to year-over-year growth by Q1 of Year 3
- **Stakeholder alignment:** Board/investor confidence maintained through transparent covenant-based reporting

The strategy balances customer retention incentives, realistic pricing architecture, and sales-force redesign to navigate the intentional revenue trough rather than hide it.

---

## 1. OFFER STRUCTURE & MIGRATION INCENTIVES

### 1.1 Segmented Migration Architecture

**Tier 1: Premium Retention Cohort (Top 20% by ARR)**
- **Target:** Existing customers generating >$50K+ annual upgrade revenue
- **Offer:** Multi-year lock-in subscription at blended rate
  - Calculate historical perpetual license cost + average upgrade spend
  - Offer 3-year subscription at 85–90% of historical total cost of ownership (TCO)
  - Guaranteed feature parity + priority support tier
  - *Rationale:* High-touch negotiations preserve anchoring customers; marginal margin loss offset by predictable retention and upsell runway

**Tier 2: Mid-Market Migration (50% of base, $10K–$50K ARR)**
- **Offer:** 2-year "bridge subscription" with optionality
  - Year 1–2: Annual subscription priced at 60% of historical annual upgrade cost
  - Embedded migration incentive: complimentary training, API access, migration services
  - End-of-Year-2 reset to standard subscription pricing (full market rate)
  - *Rationale:* Aligns with budget cycles, reduces sticker shock, creates natural renewal event with pricing reset

**Tier 3: SMB & Long-Tail (30% of base, <$10K ARR)**
- **Offer:** Freemium-to-subscription gradient
  - Free tier with core features (no time limit)
  - Entry subscription ($99–$199/month) with upsell to premium tiers
  - Discontinue perpetual license sales; shift long-tail to self-serve
  - *Rationale:* Eliminates legacy support burden; captures SMB segment at scale with lower CAC

### 1.2 Non-Subscription Retention Options (Last Resort)

**Extended Perpetual License Window**
- Open 6-month window (Months 1–6 of transition) for final perpetual purchases at 20% premium
- Enforce strict end-of-support date (18 months post-sale)
- Restricts to existing customers only; not marketed to new logos
- *Rationale:* Acknowledges installed-base psychology; creates urgency while limiting long-tail perpetual debt

**Hybrid "License + SaaS" Bundling** (Enterprise Only)
- Perpetual on-premise license + optional cloud subscription
- Separate pricing; cloud subscription positioned as ancillary (analytics, integration hub, managed updates)
- No discount for bundling; forces clear ROI case per component
- *Rationale:* Preserves control narrative for large enterprises; generates incremental SaaS revenue without cannibalizing licenses

### 1.3 Anti-Churn Mechanics

**Early-Mover Incentives (Months 1–6)**
| Cohort | Incentive | Duration |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| Tier 1 (Premium) | 15% discount + 12-mo free premium support | 3 years |
| Tier 2 (Mid-Market) | 10% discount + complimentary migration | 2 years |
| Tier 3 (SMB) | 50% off first 6 months (freemium upsell) | 6 months |

**Loyalty Bonuses**
- Customers with 5+ year tenure: additional 5% discount on subscription or 10% account credit for annual prepayment
- Referral incentive: $5K credit per net-new subscription customer referred
- *Rationale:* Converts switching risk into competitive moat; leverages high-tenure segments as advocates

**Transparent Sunset Communication**
- Announce 24-month support end-of-life for perpetual licenses (published roadmap)
- Provide 12-month advance notice before feature freeze
- Offer buyout: 1-time 30-day offer to convert to subscription at locked-in rate if customer hasn't renewed by Month 18
- *Rationale:* Reduces ambiguity; triggers decision-making without appearing punitive

### 1.4 Projected Retention & Subscription Adoption

| Cohort | Baseline Size | Projected Conversion | Residual Churn | Net Retention |
|--------|---------------|----------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Tier 1 (Premium) | 20% | 90% | 5% | 85% |
| Tier 2 (Mid) | 50% | 70% | 15% | 59.5% |
| Tier 3 (SMB) | 30% | 45% | 25% | 33.75% |
| **Blended Installed Base** | **100%** | **68%** | **15%** | **68%** (vs. 75% churn target) |

*Note:* Tiered approach limits total churn to **17.3%** through disproportionate retention of high-value cohorts.

---

## 2. SUBSCRIPTION PRICING ARCHITECTURE

### 2.1 Pricing Model Design

**Three-Tier Subscription Stack**

**Tier A: Essentials** ($49–$99/month per user or $499–$999/month for org)
- Core feature set (equivalent to current base license + 1 upgrade cycle)
- Cloud hosted only; no on-premise option
- Support: Business hours, ticket-based
- Billing: Monthly, annual (15% discount)
- Target: SMB, new customers, freemium graduates

**Tier B: Professional** ($199–$399/month per user or $1,999–$3,999/month for org)
- Full feature set + API access + integrations
- Hybrid cloud/on-premise options
- Support: 24/5, priority queue, dedicated Slack channel
- Billing: Monthly or annual (20% discount)
- Target: Mid-market, existing Tier 2 segment

**Tier C: Enterprise** (Custom)
- Unlimited features + dedicated success manager
- Full on-premise + multi-cloud options
- Support: 24/7, SLA-backed
- Billing: Annual only, volume discounts (3-year agreements typical)
- Target: Tier 1 premium segment, net-new enterprise

### 2.2 Pricing Calibration Against Trough Mitigation

**Baseline Perpetual License Revenue Model (Pre-Transition)**
- Annual license bookings: $50M
- Annual upgrade revenue: $15M (30% of base on rolling 3-year cycle)
- Total: $65M recurring-equivalent annual run rate

**Year 1–2 Subscription Revenue Projection**

| Metric | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Perpetual license bookings (declining) | $25M | $8M | $1M |
| Perpetual upgrade revenue (installed base) | $12M | $8M | $2M |
| New subscription bookings | $18M | $28M | $35M |
| Converted customer subscription revenue | $8M | $16M | $22M |
| **Total Bookings** | **$63M** | **$60M** | **$60M** |
| Recognized Revenue (ASC 606) | $58M | $62M | $65M |
| YoY Growth | -11% | +7% | +5% |

*Assumptions:*
- Perpetual license selling stops Month 7; final sales through Month 12
- Net subscription churn: 8% annually (lower than perpetual upgrade attrition)
- Subscription ARPU: $1,200–$1,500/year (blended across tiers)
- New customer acquisition ramps: $3M (M1), $5M (M6), $7M (M12), $10M+ (Y2)

**Trough Depth Analysis**
- Bookings dip 11% in Year 1 (controlled vs. peer benchmark of -25%)
- Revenue dip muted to -5% due to ASC 606 ratable recognition (vs. cliff risk of -20%+ if all licenses expired immediately)
- Inflection: Year 2 bookings recover to baseline; Year 3 exceed baseline

### 2.3 Pricing Elasticity & Adoption Targets

**Pricing Sensitivity by Cohort**

| Cohort | Historical License Cost | Bridge Subscription Offer | Adoption Sensitivity | Elasticity |
|--------|-------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------|------------|
| Premium (Tier 1) | $150K–$500K/yr | $130K–$425K/yr (87%) | Inelastic (switching cost high) | -0.15 |
| Mid-Market (Tier 2) | $25K–$100K/yr | $15K–$60K/yr (60% Y1-2) | Elastic (budget-conscious) | -0.45 |
| SMB (Tier 3) | $5K–$25K/yr | $2K–$8K/yr ($200–$800/mo) | Highly elastic (freemium competition) | -0.8 |

**Price Optimization Thresholds**
- If Tier 1 conversion falls below 80%, increase discount by 5% (vs. budgeted 15%)
- If Tier 2 adoption falls below 60% by Month 6, reduce bridge-year pricing by 10%
- If Tier 3 churn exceeds 30%, offer 50% freemium → Essentials upsell credit ($50/month voucher)

### 2.4 Annual Price Escalation & Lock-In Strategy

**Migration Cohort Pricing Lock**
- Tier 1: Price-locked for 3 years; escalates 3% annually post-year-3
- Tier 2: Price-locked for 2 years; escalates 5% annually post-year-2
- Tier 3: No lock-in; monthly pricing, market-rate escalation at renewal

*Rationale:* Lock-in reduces churn risk during transition; escalation curve reflects differentiated urgency and switching costs.

**Volume & Commitment Discounts** (New & Renewed)
- 1-year prepay: 15% discount
- 2-year prepay: 20% discount
- 3-year prepay: 25% discount (enterprise only)

---

## 3. SALES COMPENSATION REDESIGN

### 3.1 Current State Problem Statement

**Legacy Perpetual License Compensation**
- Commission structure: 15% of perpetual license bookings + 5% of upgrade upsell
- Deal cycles: 3–6 months; large upfront commissions on signature
- Incentive misalignment: Reps optimize for license volume, not customer longevity
- Revenue volatility: Commission pool fluctuates 30–40% YoY

**Transition Risks**
- Reps resist moving deals to subscriptions (8–12 month payoff vs. immediate commission)
- Churn in Q2–Q3 of Year 1 as reps optimize for commission volume over customer fit
- High-performing reps (leveraged on large perpetual deals) face 40–60% compensation reduction

### 3.2 Redesigned Subscription-Aligned Compensation Model

**Core Commission Structure (Effective Month 1)**

| Component | Perpetual License | Subscription | Multi-Year |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------|-----------|
| **Upfront Commission Rate** | 15% | 8% | 10% |
| **Annual Renewal Commission** | N/A | 3% (Year 1–2), 2% (Y3+) | N/A |
| **Churn Penalty (Clawback)** | N/A | -15% of renewal if churned | -10% of blended |
| **Expansion Commission** | Upgrade only (5%) | Net expansion ARR (6–8%) | Full + expansion (5%) |

**Rationale:**
- Lower upfront commission on subscriptions compensated by renewal revenue stream
- Churn penalty aligns rep behavior with retention (no incentive to over-sell misfit customers)
- Expansion commission rewards upselling existing subscription base (high-margin growth)
- Multi-year deals (3-year locked-in): Blended 10% rate recognizes booking size while deferring payout

### 3.3 Payout Mechanics & Transition Buffers

**Accelerated Ramp for Subscription Mastery** (Months 1–12)
- Reps hitting 70%+ of new bookings as subscriptions: +2% bonus on all comp (temporary, 12-month window)
- Reps achieving <10% churn in managed book: +$10K quarterly bonus pool (split per cohort)
- Early-mover incentive: First rep to convert Top 50 customers to subscription gets $50K bonus

**Perpetual License Holdout Protection** (Months 1–18)
- Revenue from perpetual license sales continues to earn legacy 15% commission (no reduction)
- Perpetual deals with embedded future subscription option earn hybrid rate: 10% upfront + 2% on eventual subscription conversion
- Ensures reps don't artificially suppress perpetual sales; allows natural market shift

**Target Total Compensation by Rep Profile**

| Profile | Baseline Annual Comp (Perpetual) | Year 1 Subscription Comp (with bonuses) | Year 2 Stabilized |
|---------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------|
| High performer ($2M+ ACV deals) | $400K–$600K | $350K–$450K (-15% adjusted for 8% upfront + renewal + bonus) | $420K–$520K |
| Mid performer ($500K–$2M) | $200K–$300K | $180K–$280K (-8% with bonus mitigation) | $210K–$310K |
| Growth performer (<$500K, high volume) | $120K–$180K | $140K–$200K (+10%, upside on expansion + freemium-to-paid) | $150K–$210K |

*Design intent:* High-performer comp dips 10–15% Year 1 but recovers by Year 2; growth performers see upside as they leverage expansion/freemium pipeline.

### 3.4 Compensation Governance & Communication

**Sales Manager Comp Alignment**
- Manager bonus pool: 30% tied to team net subscription adoption %; 30% to blended churn rate; 40% to total bookings
- Removes perverse incentive to pump perpetual deals at expense of subscription migration
- Creates cascading accountability for retention and customer fit

**Transparent Comp Comms & Guardrails**
- Month 0: All-hands comp roadshow; document transition timeline, rate cards, examples (typical deal impact: -10% to +20% depending on deal mix)
- Month 1–6: Weekly comp reporting dashboard (deal pipeline by type, projected commission, bonus tracker)
- Month 6 check-in: Mid-year review; reps 15%+ below Year 1 target get supplemental bonus pool ($500K discretionary)
- Escalation path: Reps can appeal comp impact with finance; escalation committee reviews cohort migration data

**Sales Ops Enablement**
- CPQ (configure-price-quote) system pre-configured with subscription models; forces rep to run comparison analysis (perpetual vs. subscription ROI for customer)
- Sales methodology training: 4-week cadence shift from deal-close to land-expand-retain playbook
- Deals desk: Enterprise team (VP Sales + CFO + Solutions Engineer) approves all deals >$500K to ensure pricing discipline and customer fit validation

### 3.5 Retention & Attrition Risk Mitigation

**Counteroffers for Top-Performing Flight Risk**
- Identify top 20% of perpetual-deal closers (Year 1); extend multi-year comp guarantees
- Guarantee: 85% of prior-year comp for Year 1, 90% for Year 2 (regardless of deal mix)
- Vesting: Conditioned on staying through Year 2 (avoid exodus mid-transition)
- Cost: ~$3M (estimated 80 reps × $37.5K guarantee) — negotiate as retention investment vs. replacement/retraining cost

**Internal Mobility / Redeployment**
- Reps struggling with subscription selling: offer field marketing, solutions engineer, or account management track (lateral moves, no comp reduction)
- Career path transparency: subscription account executives can earn $300K+ by Year 2 (vs. legacy deal-close model capping at $200K)
- Upskilling stipend: $5K per rep for CRM/subscription sales certifications

---

## 4. FINANCIAL COMMUNICATION STRATEGY FOR BOARD & INVESTORS

### 4.1 Messaging Framework: "Transition vs. Trough"

**Core Narrative**

> *"We are managing a deliberate transition from lumpy, discounted-cash-flow revenue to predictable, recurring subscription revenue. The near-term revenue trough (12–18 months, 5–11% dip) is a temporary effect of converting installed base at lower entry prices; we emerge into a higher-quality revenue base with 40%+ gross margin, <10% net churn, and 3-year visible pipeline. This transition positions us for 20%+ annual growth in Year 3–5 and a 60%+ Rule of 40 score by Year 4."*

**Key Credibility Anchors**
- Quantify trough depth: "Our bridge-pricing model limits Year 1 bookings decline to 11% vs. peer benchmark of 25%"
- Highlight leading indicators: Subscription penetration targets (Month 6: 40%, Month 12: 60%, Month 24: 75%+)
- Commitment to board covenants: Covenant-based reporting ensures early warning if churn exceeds thresholds

### 4.2 Board & Investor Covenant Structure

**Monthly Reporting Dashboards** (Shared with Board Finance & Investor Relations)

**Tier 1: Strategic Health Indicators** (Green/Yellow/Red flags)
| KPI | Baseline / Target | Green Threshold | Yellow Threshold | Red Flag | Frequency |
|-----|-------------------|-----------------|-----------------|----------|-----------|
| **Subscription Bookings % of New** | N/A → 60% (M12) | >55% of target | 50–55% of target | <50% of target | Weekly |
| **Installed Base Churn Rate** | Baseline 12% → 8% (Y2) | <12% Y1, <10% Y2 | 12–14% Y1 | >14% Y1 | Monthly |
| **Blended Net Dollar Retention** | Baseline 95% → 105% (Y2) | >100% | 95–100% | <95% | Quarterly |
| **Year 1 Total Bookings** | $63M ± 5% | $60M–$66M | $55M–$60M | <$55M | Monthly |
| **Conversion Rate: Tier 1 Customers** | Target 90% | >85% | 80–85% | <80% | Monthly |

**Tier 2: Financial Health (Quarterly)**
- Gross margin by segment (perpetual vs. subscription)
- Magic number (incremental ARR / sales & marketing spend) trend
- Cash burn: months of runway by scenario (base, downside, upside)
- Annual recurring revenue (ARR) and ARR growth rate

**Tier 3: Operational Health (Quarterly)**
- Sales rep productivity: new subscription bookings per FTE
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback period (target: 18–24 months)
- Sales compensation cost as % of subscription bookings (target: 35–40%)

### 4.3 Scenario Planning & Downside Communication

**Base, Downside, & Upside Cases** (Shared Q1 Board Meeting; updated quarterly)

| Scenario | Assumption Drivers | Year 1 Bookings | Year 2 Bookings | Year 3 Revenue | Year 3 EBITDA Margin | Probability |
|----------|-------------------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Base** | 68% conversion, 12% churn, $1.3K ARPU | $63M | $60M | $65M | 35% | 60% |
| **Upside** | 75% conversion, 10% churn, $1.5K ARPU | $68M | $72M | $80M | 38% | 20% |
| **Downside** | 55% conversion, 15% churn, $1.0K ARPU | $55M | $48M | $52M | 30% | 20% |

**Downside Contingency Triggers & Actions**

| Trigger | Action | Timeline |
|---------|--------|----------|
| Tier 2 conversion falls <60% (Month 6) | 1) Reduce bridge-year pricing by 10%; 2) Extend incentive window 3 months | Immediate |
| Installed base churn exceeds 14% (Month 3) | 1) Activate Tier 1 rescue program (CEO outreach); 2) Extend perpetual support end-of-life date 6 months | Month 3 |
| Year 1 bookings track <$57M (Month 9) | 1) Accelerate new customer CAC investment; 2) Reduce OpEx by 5% (hiring freeze); 3) Consider strategic M&A of subscription-native competitor | Month 9 |
| Net dollar retention <95% (Q2) | 1) Launch win-back program for churned customers; 2) Increase support tier bundling in new deals | Q2 |

### 4.4 Board Presentation Cadence & Talking Points

**Pre-Announcement Board Meeting (Month -1): Authorization & Alignment**

**Agenda:**
1. Transition rationale: Market headwinds (revenue volatility discount) vs. opportunity (20%+ SaaS multiples)
2. Risk acknowledgment: Peer benchmarks, trough quantification, churn containment levers
3. Covenant approval: Board votes to adopt monthly reporting cadence; authorizes <20% churn covenant
4. Compensation guardrails: Board pre-approves $3M retention pool + modified commission structure
5. Decision: Explicit board authorization to "communicate transition to investors on roadshow"

**Q1 Board Meeting (Month 1): Launch & Commitment**

**Talking points:**
- "We've launched migration in controlled fashion: Tier 1 (premium) conversion tracking 85% vs. 90% target—ahead of plan."
- "Churn prevention mechanics are working: bridge pricing resonates with mid-market; freemium strategy reducing SMB support burden by 15%."
- "New subscription bookings pipeline: $18M in Month 1–2, 40% of plan already visible for Year 1."
- "Covenant health: On track for <12% Year 1 churn. Monthly reporting beginning next month."
- "Year 1 trough: Modeling $63M bookings (vs. $65M baseline), 3% decline—accretive to long-term value."

**Q2 Board Meeting (Month 3): Mid-Course Correction & Investor Prep**

**Talking points (if tracking to plan):**
- "Tier 1 conversion now 88% (cumulative); Tier 2 at 68% (slight upside vs. 70% target)."
- "Net churn: 10.5% installed base (within covenant range)."
- "New subscription pipeline tracking $22M YTD, still on pace for $60M+ bookings."
- "Board dashboard: 4 of 5 green-flag KPIs; 1 yellow (expansion revenue from installed base lower-than-expected—addressing with account management ramp)."
- "Investor message refined: Emphasize trough as planned, demonstrate control via covenants, highlight Year 2–3 inflection."

**Q3 & Q4 Board Meetings (Months 6, 9): Variance Analysis & Next Year Outlook**

**Talking points (contingent on performance):**
- Quantify cumulative churn vs. covenants; project Year 2 ARR run rate
- Highlight new customer cohort quality: CAC payback, initial net dollar retention (leading indicator)
- Re-forecast Year 1 bookings with 9-month actuals; update 3-year guidance
- Address investor questions: "When does bookings growth turn positive?" (Answer: Q2 of Year 2, with conservative assumptions already built in)

### 4.5 Investor Communication & Road Show Strategy

**Pre-Announcement Investor Messaging (Month -1)**

**Goal:** Pre-frame narrative before formal announcement to prevent negative surprise

**Approach:**
- CFO / Investor Relations: Selective calls to top 10 institutional investors + sell-side analysts
- Message: "We're transitioning business model to better align with SaaS market multiples. Managed carefully to preserve cash flow and customer relationships. We'll provide detailed roadmap + monthly reporting to demonstrate control."
- Timing: 1 week before public announcement
- Outcome: Neutralize surprise; set expectation for trough; frame as value-creation lever

**Public Announcement & Earnings Call (Month 1)**

**Talking points:**
- Headline: "Subscription Transition Underway—Targeting <20% Churn, 60%+ Adoption by Month 12"
- Key metrics: Bridge pricing strategy, covenant structure, Year 1 guidance (63M bookings)
- Credibility: Peer benchmarks (Competitor X lost 25% base, we're architecting for <20%)
- Finish with: "Monthly reporting to investors beginning February. Dashboard covers leading indicators to ensure transparency during transition."

**Quarterly Earnings Calls (Post-Announcement)**

**Q1 Call (Month 3):**
- "Transition is on track: Tier 1 conversion 88%, churn 10.5%, subscription bookings 38% of new."
- "We're ahead of plan on customer retention; trailing on new customer acquisition (within forecast range)."
- "No guidance change; reaffirm Year 1 bookings of $63M ± 5%."

**Q2 Call (Month 6):**
- Introduce covenant scorecard: "4 of 5 KPIs in green; 1 yellow (expansion revenue). Addressed with account management hiring."
- "Year 2 guidance: $60M bookings (base case), with visible upside if subscription penetration exceeds 65% (now tracking at 55%)."
- "Cash flow: Transition results in $2–3M incremental cash burn vs. standalone perpetual model, offset by reduced CapEx. Runway: 48 months at current burn."

**Q3 & Q4 Calls (Months 9, 12):**
- Shift tone: "Trough now behind us. Year 2 bookings trajectory clear from pipeline visibility."
- Highlight: "New customer cohorts are stickier (8% net churn vs. 12% blended base). Expansion revenue accelerating."
- Guidance: "Year 2 bookings: $60M–$64M, with Year 3 inflection to $65M+. EBITDA margin path: 25% (Y1) → 32% (Y2) → 38% (Y3)."

### 4.6 Analyst & Media Strategy

**Analyst Coverage Approach**
- Dedicate IR resource to educate analysts on SaaS transition metrics (magic number, net dollar retention, CAC payback)
- Proactive outreach: Schedule post-earnings calls with sell-side software analysts to walk through model assumptions
- Provide bridge model: Perpetual license depreciation schedule + subscription ARR build, showing Path to $100M+ revenue by Year 5

**Media / PR Strategy**
- Embargo release: Announce transition to industry press (Software Equity Group, Forrester, Gartner) 1 day before earnings
- Frame as: "Subscription Transition Positioned to Unlock SaaS Multiples; Managed Churn Strategy Differentiates from Peer Failures"
- Customer testimonial: Secure 2–3 Tier 1 customer quotes for announcement ("This is the right direction for our long-term partnership")

### 4.7 Communication Cadence Summary

| Audience | Frequency | Content | Owner |
|----------|-----------|---------|-------|
| **Board of Directors** | Monthly (dashboard), Quarterly (meeting) | KPI tracker, scenario updates, covenant health | CFO |
| **Institutional Investors** | Quarterly (earnings call), Ad-hoc (major variance) | Earnings materials, detailed financials, transition milestones | CEO / CFO / IR |
| **Sell-Side Analysts** | Quarterly (post-earnings), As-needed (models) | Model updates, transition mechanics, 3-year guidance | IR / CFO |
| **Employees (Sales/Ops)** | Monthly (all-hands), Weekly (sales force) | Comp performance, customer conversions, churn trends, incentive payouts | Sales leadership / HR |
| **Customers** | Ongoing (account teams), Quarterly (exec business reviews) | Subscription roadmap, support commitments, renewal management | Customer success / Sales |

---

## 5. INTEGRATED TRANSITION TIMELINE & SUCCESS METRICS

### 5.1 30-60-90 Rollout Plan

**Months 1–2: Foundation & Communication**
- [ ] Announce transition to board, investors, employees, customers
- [ ] Finalize offer tiers, pricing, migration incentives (Tier 1–3)
- [ ] Launch sales training: subscription selling playbook, CPQ configuration, deal desk approval process

# STRATEGY 1: EXISTING CUSTOMERS — MIGRATION INCENTIVE DESIGN

## Behavioral Economics Foundation

**Psychological Drivers of Churn Risk**
1. **Loss Aversion (Kahneman-Tversky):** Customers perceive perpetual license as "owned asset"; subscription feels like "rental loss"
   - *Manifestation:* "I already paid for this license; why should I rent?"
   - *Behavioral lever:* Reframe as "upgrade, not replacement"; design "fairness credit" against new subscription
   
2. **Sunk Cost Fallacy:** Historical license investment creates entitlement narrative
   - *Manifestation:* Resistance to migration pricing, even if TCO-neutral
   - *Behavioral lever:* Acknowledge sunk cost explicitly; offer "loyalty bonus" tied to tenure, not pricing
   
3. **Status Quo Bias:** Perpetual license = known; subscription = uncertain
   - *Manifestation:* Inertia; delay decision-making; default to churn if friction is high
   - *Behavioral lever:* Reduce decision friction (pre-approved offers, one-click migration, dedicated account team)
   
4. **Fairness & Reciprocity (Fehr-Gächter):** Customers expect fair treatment in exchange for loyalty
   - *Manifestation:* Resentment if they perceive company "punishing" early customers
   - *Behavioral lever:* Transparent communication of why transition benefits them; frame incentives as "recognition," not "discount"
